items.title: DR Congo: WHO urges sustained efforts as Ebola cases top 10,000
items.summary: As Ebola cases in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) surpass the 10,000 mark, the World Health Organization (WHO) has underlined the need for continued efforts to contain spread of the disease.

items.title: Protecting the storytellers: Women journalists on the frontline of conflict
items.summary: As online abuse, gender-based attacks and impunity ramp up the threats to women reporting from crisis zones, journalists and UN leaders are calling for urgent action to protect those who document conflict.

items.title: Ending conflict is ‘number one thing’ to reduce world hunger, new WFP chief says
items.summary: Reducing conflict is the single most effective way to tackle global hunger, the new head of the UN World Food Programme (WFP), Luke Lindberg, said on Wednesday, noting that conflict drives two thirds of the acute food insecurity affecting 266 million people worldwide.

items.title: Backing for UN call to end Cuba embargo falls to 20-year low
items.summary: The UN General Assembly on Wednesday called for the 34th time for an end to the US economic, commercial and financial embargo on Cuba – but with the weakest backing for the resolution in two decades.

items.title: UN human rights chief urges better protection of civilians in conflicts
items.summary: Youth-led protests against corruption and inequality in Serbia, Bangladesh, Nepal and Madagascar reflect a growing demand for reinforcing human rights around the world, UN human rights chief Volker Türk said at a press briefing on Wednesday.

items.title: Civilians in Sudan’s El Obeid trapped between drones and incarceration
items.summary: Civilians in Sudan’s El Obeid live in constant fear of drone attacks by the Rapid Support Forces (RSF) and of a wave of arbitrary arrests by the Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF), UN-appointed independent investigators said on Wednesday.

items.title: Security Council LIVE: Women and girls face greater dangers in war
